about: Plans with known answers. expect_findings: rule findings that must be detected (warning or critical for all but info rules). correct_fix_types: option types that fix the problem; an empty list means Jev should decline. Add your own anonymized plans in fixtures/eval/private/ with the same cases.json shape.

cases.description: Key lookup executed 60,000 times from a narrow nonclustered index.
Plan compiled for a rare status value, reused for a common one.
nvarchar parameter against a varchar column forces a scan.
Sort spills because 1,200 rows were estimated and 1.5 million arrived.
Ascending-key statistics are 4.2 million modifications old; the recent range is estimated at 10 rows.
Estimated plan: clustered scan reads 3 million rows to return 420; the optimizer suggests an index.
cases.why: Estimated plan: the index is the fix, but capturing the actual plan first (ops) is the safer first action with no runtime evidence.

cases.description: A scalar UDF runs per row and forces a serial plan.
cases.why: Inlining the function by hand (rewrite) or enabling scalar UDF inlining (ops, compatibility level 150+) both remove the per-row calls.

cases.description: A table variable estimated at 1 row holds 250,000; nested loops run 250,000 seeks.
A single-row clustered seek: nothing to fix. Declining to pick is the right answer.
One parallel thread reads 1.9 million rows while seven read 15,000 each; CXPACKET dominates.
The optimizer builds a temporary index over Orders on every run because no index on CustomerId includes Total.
YEAR(OrderDate) = 2025 scans an index that a date-range predicate could seek.
A one-row update that waited 29.5 seconds on a lock: the plan is fine, another session was blocking.
TOP 10 made the optimizer expect to stop after 50 orders; it read 1.8 million because EMEA customers are rare.
Sorting 900,000 rows is 87% of the time; an index on (Status, OrderDate) delivers them in order.
A filtered index on Status = 'Open' exists but a parameterized query cannot use it.
The filter runs locally after pulling 3 million rows across a linked server.

Month-end report batch: 3 statements; the main one joins 7 tables at DOP 8, runs 48 s with 210 s CPU. A key lookup runs 6.3 million times (the largest own time), the plan was compiled for a different segment and date range, a hash join spills because 1,200 customers were estimated and 480,000 arrived, one thread does 69% of the Orders scan, statistics are stale, and Segment is implicitly converted.
A covering-index seek returning 12 rows waited 20.9 s on LCK_M_S: a writer in another session held the lock. The plan is already optimal.
An ORM sends the email as nvarchar(4000) against a varchar(256) indexed column: the column is converted, so IX_Customers_Email is scanned (3.2 million rows) instead of sought.
Cancelled by a 30 s client timeout: the scan of 240 million Events had read 96 million rows looking for one customer when it stopped. The plan is partial.
Archiving 4.8 million orders in one INSERT ... SELECT: 96 s, 41 s waiting on WRITELOG, a sort that spills to maintain three nonclustered indexes on the target.
